end.summary:
Practised the structure of India’s courts and the idea of appeal.
Distinguished civil and criminal cases using property disputes and theft.
Explored FIR, investigation, the role of the state, and public order in criminal cases.
Teach-back was not passed; no misconceptions were recorded.
end.parentNote: Vihaan practised sorting examples into civil and criminal cases and tracing an appeal from a District Court to the High Court and Supreme Court. They explained that crime can affect the wider society and that the state helps maintain public order. They repeatedly asked for drawings and clearer visual examples; at the end, they identified a plot-boundary dispute as a civil case. At home, ask them to make a three-level court flowchart and label one example at each level.
